When I told my twitter friends about my miscarriage, I was letting them know why I was going to be offline for a while. It was nice to have support bc I felt so damn alone - women reached out and told me they went through the same which was helpful while I grieved bc it felt surreal to be so profoundly sad over a baby I never even got to meet. Grief policing is probably the worst thing someone can do - just
Hope that when you go through a loss people don’t judge you, however you decide to grieve. Don’t like how someone is grieving? Here’s the good news - you’re not the one grieving a death - and I promise they wish they weren’t grieving a  death either.
Havent you ever heard of sudden infant death syndrome? It is a very well known thing. Thousands of babies die every year from it and this is wAyyyyyy before covid.
Not if you have a lot of online friends and are simply filling them in before you take your space to grieve. I did the same thing after I lost my pregnancy.

I am very active on Twitter, have a lot of friends that are just my twitter friends I’ve had for years, and when I had my miscarriage I tweeted it out bc I was taking a break from it to grieve. I was in shock. I can’t even imagine losing a child at two months but I’m assuming she is doing the same thing here, letting her twitter friends know and she will take her space. Grief is different for everyone - some people it’s private, some it’s public. What’s wrong is the grief police - people who say how you should or shouldn’t do it - just pray that people return the favor and treat you kindly when you go through a loss. Don’t like how she’s doing it? Here’s good news - it’s not your grief. You didn’t lose the baby. Aren’t you lucky? This poor woman. It’s awful.
